title: Quadruples With a Given Sum

concept.title: Fix two numbers, then two pointers
body: This is the three-sum idea one level deeper. After sorting, fix the first number `a[i]` and the second number `a[j]`; the remaining two must add up to `target - a[i] - a[j]`, which two pointers `l` and `r` find in O(n). Two nested loops times a linear scan give O(n^3).
To count each combination of values once, skip equal neighbours at all four levels: at the first and second number when starting the loop body, and at the third (and fourth) after a hit.

statement: Given `n` integers and a number `target`, count the different quadruples of **values** `(w, x, y, z)` with `w <= x <= y <= z` and `w + x + y + z = target`. Two quadruples are the same if they contain the same values; the four elements must come from four different positions.
outputFormat: Print the number of different quadruples.
hints: Fix the first two numbers with two loops and find the other two with two pointers.
Skip repeated values at every level so that a quadruple of values is counted once.

solution.complexity: Time O(n^3), space O(1) besides sorting.
